claims.title: Bounds-checked string and list access
claims.statement: For programs compiled as Capstan, string and list indexing outside the valid range is detected and terminates safely rather than performing an out-of-bounds access.
scope: Capstan-language programs compiled by the repository compiler
String and list indexing operations covered by the language specification and runtime
assumptions: The Capstan compiler and generated-code checks behave as specified.
The C compiler, C runtime, operating system and platform C library are within the trusted computing base.
dependencies: The selected C compiler and platform C library
limitations: This claim does not establish memory safety of the C runtime itself.
It does not cover future foreign-function interfaces or unsafe platform extensions.
A test fixture's presence is not evidence that it passed on the snapshot revision.
read_file is regular-file-only and rejects non-regular sources before reading; synchronous stdin operations may still wait indefinitely and have no deadline guarantee.

claims.title: C-free scalar type-safety proof profile
claims.statement: For the explicitly scoped C-free scalar profile, Capstan is developing a compositional type-safety argument from checked source through CCAM validation and execution to native code; current machine-checked evidence covers only a restricted typed CCAM model, not the complete implementation pipeline.
scope: C-free scalar source subset: int, bool, locals, expressions, structured control flow, direct calls and returns
CCAM typed machine, validator, Capstan-native evaluator and experimental native backend
assumptions: The formal models are not treated as implementation proofs without explicit refinement theorems.
The legacy generated-C backend is excluded from the proof target and used only as a temporary differential comparator.
limitations: The Lean machine is a restricted single-frame model and does not yet formalise the executable multi-function call-frame evaluator.
The formal validator is a conservative in-memory single-frame proof profile, not the complete normative CCAM validator or JSON decoder.
Source checker soundness and source-to-CCAM semantic preservation are not established.
The native register bridge proves mathematical representation lemmas, not full concrete evaluator or native code refinement.
Strings, heap, collections, optionals, taint, secrets, grants, IO, concurrency and FFI are outside this profile.
The proposed reference-identity, collector and generational-handle models added in #426 do not extend the supported C-free scalar profile and do not establish compiler/runtime refinement.

The aggregate register/heap bridge introduced in #492 is an experimental reference transition model, not canonical CCAM, not in the supported scalar profile, and not a native-backend or production-front-end refinement proof.

evidence.procedure: Review the stated profile, proof ladder, exclusions and implementation correspondence boundaries.
evidence.notes: C-free assurance contract and compatibility boundary, including the experimental aggregate bridge's explicit non-goals; not a claim of completed end-to-end verification. Artifact inventory refreshed at reconciled source revision; no new passing test result asserted. C02 adds AST arity, literal domain and result-type rejection; malformed-node regression tests added. No new proof or passing exact-head test asserted. Direct ELF now has a bounded scalar call profile (15 registers/function, 16 frames including entry, 256 relocation labels) and record-mode parameterless void entry. The added execution vectors provide test evidence for calls, recursion/depth traps, terminal records and arena operations; they do not establish native-code refinement, stable ABI, or whole-program equivalence.
